titleEn: Laws of Hammurabi — Epilogue IV: the last curses (xliii 81 – xliv 91)

draftNote: The § chips number the laws (Harper’s sectioning, still standard); long laws span several tap-units. Readings checked sign-by-sign against Harper’s 1904 edition.
source: Louvre stele, after R.F. Harper, The Code of Hammurabi, King of Babylon (Chicago, 1904): transliteration and autograph plates, List of Signs. Readings are Harper’s in modern subscript notation. Cuneiform in Old Babylonian monumental sign forms via the SantakkuM webfont by Sylvie Vanséveren (CC BY 4.0); pronunciation: conventional reconstructed Old Babylonian. Audio: a German synthetic voice reads the Akkadian word by word from these pronunciation rules (word stress after Huehnergard). It cannot hold a consonant long, so doubled consonants are heard single (šumma with one m), and the emphatics ṭ and q are heard as plain t and k. Fresh translations made directly from the Akkadian; Harper’s public-domain translation consulted for sense only.

about: The fourth and last part of the epilogue finishes the curses on a later king who destroys or alters the stele, and with it the stele and the code. Zamama, the warrior at the king’s right hand, is asked to break the wrongdoer’s weapon in battle, turn his day into night and set his enemy over him (xliii 81–91). Ištar, lady of battle, is asked, in her anger, to curse his kingship, to turn his good into evil, to set confusion and revolt on him, to make his warriors fall and the earth drink their blood, to heap his army’s corpses in the open country and to give him bound into his enemy’s hand (xliii 92 – xliv 23). Nergal, the strong one among the gods, is asked to burn his people like a fire in a reed-bed, to bring him to an end with his strong weapon (?) and to smash his body like a clay figure (xliv 24–39). Nintu is asked to take a son and a name from him and to let him beget no seed (xliv 40–49). Ninkarrak, the daughter of Anum, is asked to send a heavy sickness on him that no physician can cure, until his life is destroyed (xliv 50–69). Last, the great gods of heaven and earth and the Anunnaki are asked to curse him, his seed, his land, his army and his people, and Ellil, with the word that is never changed, to curse him and let the curse overtake him quickly (xliv 70–91). This is the end of the text on the stele. The stele is read through Harper’s 1904 transliteration and his plates; a number of words in these curses are rare, the readings are his or mine, and the notes say where they are uncertain.

sentences.i: Zamama, the great warrior, the first son (?) of Ekur, who goes at my right hand,
sentences.n: A new god, and a new paragraph of curses. {d}za-ma₃-ma₃ is Zamama: the god’s name spelled with the signs ZA, MA₃, MA₃, as at xl 22 (Harper prints ZA.MA(L).MA(L), and his sign list shows the same group), after the silent divine determinative AN. qarrādum rabûm is “the great warrior”, two nominatives in -um; the first sign is GAR, read qar (Harper prints it gar here and qar at xliv 8). mār rēštûm: Harper prints mar+ri-eš-tu-um as one word, with a plus where the plate shows a cross-like mark; I read mar “son” and rēštûm “first, foremost” (the adjective of the glossary), so “the first son”. That this means “first-born son” is UNCERTAIN, and so is the division into two words. ša Ekur is “of Ekur”, Enlil’s temple (É.KUR, as at xlii 81). ālik imnīya “who goes at my right”: ālik is the participle of alākum, written a-li-ku with the -u kept before the genitive (as mušarriku at xlii 101), and imnīya is imittum “right side” + -ia, “my right”: the god who walks beside the king as his helper. The wishes follow in the next two units.

sentences.i: in the place of battle may he break his weapon,
sentences.n: ašar tamḫārim “in the place of battle”: ašar is ašrum “place” in the construct, and tamḫārim is “of battle” (tamḫārum, spelled tam-ḫa-ri-im with the UD sign read tam). kakkašu “his weapon”: GIŠ.TUKUL is the Sumerogram for kakkum with no ending written (as kakkim at xl 22), then the sign ŠU “his”; the second sign is keyed TUK, as in epilogue-1 (TENTATIVE). lišbir “let him break” is the precative of šebērum “to break” (the glossary has the preterite išbir). The subject is still Zamama; as in the other curses, a wish for the ruin of the king who destroys the stele.

sentences.i: may he turn the day into night for him, and set his enemy up against him.
sentences.n: ūmam “the day” (accusative): UD with the ending written out, -ma-am; Harper’s û is the UD sign, as in epilogue-3 at xliii 1. ana mūšim “into night” (mūšum “night”, mu-ši-im). litēršumma is the D precative of târum + -šum “for him” + -ma “and”: with ana “into” it means “turn (day) into night for him”. At xliii 1 and 45 (epilogue-3) the same verb has -šu “from him” and was rendered “turn away from him” (UNCERTAIN there as here). nakiršu elīšu lišziz “let him set his enemy up against him”: nakiršu is nakrum “enemy” + -šu, elīšu is eli “over, against” + -šu, and lišziz is the Š precative of izuzzum “to stand”, “let him make (his enemy) stand”. The curse of Zamama ends with this unit.

sentences.n: ana qāt nakrišu “into the hand of his enemy” (qāt, spelled qa₂-at; Harper prints ga-at; nakrum + -šu). limallišuma is the D precative of malûm “to fill” + -šu “him” + -ma “and”; the D stem, with ana qāt, is the idiom “to hand over to”. ana māt nukurtišu “to the land of his hostility”, that is, his enemy’s land (as ina māt nukurtim in the glossary; nukurtum “enmity”). kamiš lirʾûšu: kamiš is an adverb in -iš, “bound, in bonds” (from kamûm “to bind”), and lirʾûšu is “let them herd him”, the precative of rêʾûm “to pasture, herd” in the 3rd plural + -šu (li-ru-šu, the ru spelling ruʾ). Both words are UNCERTAIN: Harper’s glossary files li-ru-šu (with li-ri, as in epilogue-2) under ARU II,1 “to carry, to rule”, and has KAMÎŠ “bound” as its own entry; I keep the house reading of that verb as rêʾûm (epilogue-2, “shepherd, rule”) and render “lead”, the shepherd’s verb for a captive. Lines 20 and 22 have second tiers on the plate (Harper’s {b}).

morph.gloss: Nergal ({d}NER.URU.GAL, the star + NER + URU + GAL; Harper’s sign list no. 170) — the strong god of battle: Nergal dannum ina ilī “Nergal, the strong one among the gods”

the strong one: ina dīnim ana dannim ištarak “in a lawsuit he handed (him) to the strong” · strong, mighty (adjective): dannim (genitive) “strong”, danniātim (da-ni-a-tim, feminine plural genitive) “mighty”

to receive: imḫur(u) · imḫur, imḫuru “he received” (preterite; subjunctive in a clause), imaḫḫar “he shall receive” (present); …ḫari… in a broken form · to face, withstand (litany): qabal lā maḫārim “combat none can face” · imtaḫar (im-ta-ḫar) “she received” (perfect; Harper’s maḫāru I,2, “to receive”): grain and silver for beer · maḫir (ma-ḫi-ir, stative, 3rd singular) “has received”: idīšu … maḫir “he has received his wage” · imaḫḫaršu (i-maḫ-ḫar-šu, present + -šu) “he shall accept from him”: the owner of the pen imaḫḫaršu the loss, “shall accept it from him”

Š-stem of kašādum: to cause to reach: uštakšidaššu “he got him back (to his city)” · mušakšidu (mu-ša-ak-ši-du, participle, the -u kept) “who brings about, who gives”: mušakšidu irnittīya “who brings about my victory”
victory (Harper’s irnittu): irnitti (ir-ni-ti, the form before a genitive) “victory of”

my · written -ia after a consonant or Sumerogram (URU-ia, ALAN-ia, utlīya, narûya); the plural nouns take -ūa or -īya (awâtūa, uṣurātūa, uṣurātīya); bare -ī in ṣillī, šumī · on a singular nominative: rēṣūa (ri-zu-u-a, ZU read ṣu) “my helper”

sentences.i: Nergal, the strong one among the gods, whose battle none can face, who brings about my victory,
sentences.n: A new god. {d}NER.URU.GAL is Nergal, written with the signs NER (keyed KIŠ), URU and GAL, as in Harper’s sign list no. 170. dannum ina ilī “the strong one among the gods” (ilī is the doubled sign NI.NI, as at xlii 22). qabal lā maḫār “battle none can face”: qabal is the construct of qablum “battle” (qa₂-ba-al; Harper prints ga-ba-al) and lā maḫār the infinitive of maḫārum “to face” with the negative (ma-ḫa-ar); the glossary has the same phrase in the genitive, qabal lā maḫārim; line 26 has a second tier on the plate (Harper’s {b}). mušakšidu irnittīya “who brings about my victory”: mušakšidu is the Š participle of kašādum “to reach” (“who makes (me) reach”), with the -u kept, as mušarriku at xlii 101; irnittīya is irnittum “victory” + -ia (the form irnitti before a genitive, then -ia).

sentences.n: A new goddess. {d}NIN.TU is Nintu “lady of birth” (the signs NIN and TU after the silent determinative). bēltum ṣīrtum “the exalted lady”: NIN is bēltum (as at xlii 81) and ṣi-ir-tum is the feminine of ṣīrum “lofty, exalted”. ša mātātim “of the lands” (mātātim, the plural of mātum, ma-ta-tim). ummum bānītī “the mother, my creator”: ummum is the sign AMA (as at xlii 81–82), bānītī is the feminine participle of banûm “to create” + -ī “my” (ba-ni-ti), “my creator” (feminine; Harper’s BANÎTU “mother”), as bānî “my creator” (masculine) at xliii 41 (epilogue-3).

sentences.i: May she turn a son away from him, and may she not let him obtain a name; may he not beget the seed of mankind among his people.
sentences.n: māram litēršuma “let her turn a son away from him, and”: māram is DUMU (the sign TUR) with the ending -am (Harper prints mâram), and litēršuma is the verb of xliii 1 and 45 (epilogue-3), “let her turn (it) away from him”, UNCERTAIN as there. Line 44 is two ruled rows on the plate with Harper’s {b}, one stele line. šumam “a name” (šumum). ay ušaršīšu “may she not let him obtain”: ay with the preterite, as in epilogue-3, of the Š stem of rašûm “to get” + -šu “him” (u-šar-ši-šu); a name is the first thing he is to be denied, after a son. ina kirbit nišīšu “in the midst of his people” (kirbit is Harper’s kirbitu “midst”, kir-bi-it, UNCERTAIN as a word; nišīšu, nišū + -šu). zēr awīlūtim “the seed of mankind”: zēr is the sign ZIR (Harper’s zêr) and awīlūtim the genitive of awīlūtum; ay ibni “may he not create (beget)”, ay with the preterite of banûm. Lines 44, 46 and 47 have second tiers on the plate (Harper’s {b}). The curse is that the wrongdoer have no offspring.

sentences.i: Ninkarrak, the daughter of Anum, who speaks of my kindness (?) in Ekur,
sentences.n: A new goddess. {d}NIN.KAR.RA.AK is Ninkarrak, written with the signs NIN, KAR, RA, AK (Harper’s name); the physician-goddess. mārat Anim “daughter of Anum”: mārat is DUMU with the ending written -at (the glossary’s mārtum), and AN.NIM is Anim, the genitive of Anum, the two signs AN and NIM. qābiat dumqīya “who speaks my favor”: qābiat is the feminine participle of qabûm “to speak” (qa₂-bi-a-at; Harper prints ga-bi-a-at), and dumqīya is dumqum “kindness, favor” + -ia (dum-qi₂-ia, KI read qi₂; Harper prints dum-ki-ia): “who speaks of my kindness”, UNCERTAIN as an idiom (Harper’s DUMKU is “favor”). ina Ekur “in Ekur” (É.KUR; Harper prints Ê with a circumflex here and plain E elsewhere). The curses follow in the next units.

sentences.i: a heavy illness, an evil ašakku, a painful wound,
sentences.n: Three accusatives, objects of lišaṣiaššumma at xliv 65. murṣam kabtam “a heavy illness” (murṣum “illness”, the HAR sign read mur; kab-tam, kabtum “heavy, severe”). ašakkam lemnam “an evil ašakku”: ašakku is the name of a sickness (a sickness-demon), written on the plate with two signs, Á (A₂) and a second sign that I do not identify; Harper’s sign list no. 129 gives the two signs together as ašakku (his glossary: ASAKKU “disease”) and draws the second as a vertical wedge with a box of bars, as on the plate; I cannot identify it. The key LAL (his no. 181, a plain hooked vertical) is only a placeholder and is not the plate’s shape, so the second sign is shown as ?; UNCERTAIN. ṣimmam marṣam “a painful wound”: ṣimmum “wound” (the sign ZI read ṣi, as in the glossary’s ṣimmam kabtam; Harper prints zi-im-ma-am), with marṣam “sick, painful”. Lines 55 and 57 each have a second tier on the plate (Harper’s {b}).

sentences.n: ina ṣimdi lā unaḫḫuššu: ṣimdi is “by a bandage” (written zi-im-di; Harper’s SIMDU “bandage”, which I follow, with ZI read ṣi as in ṣimmum), and lā unaḫḫuššu is unaḫḫuš, the D present of naḫûm “to be quiet” (Harper’s NAḪU II,1 “to pacify, to allay”; D, “to give ease to”), + -šu “him”, the š of the stem and the š of -šu written once (u-na-aḫ-ḫu-šu, split over two tiers on the plate); the subject is the physician of the last unit. kīma nišiq mūtim lā innassaḫu “like the bite of death that is not removed”: nišiq is the construct of nišqum (Harper’s NIŠQU “bite”, written ni-ši-iq with the IG sign read iq), so “the bite of death”; it is not našāqum “to kiss”, and the exact sense is UNCERTAIN. mūtim is “of death” (mūtum, with long ū; mutum “husband” is a different word), and innassaḫu is the N present of nasāḫum “to pull out, remove” with the -u of the clause (in-na-za-ḫu, with za for -ssa- as in the glossary’s innassaḫ): the sickness cannot be pulled out of him.

sentences.n: ana idlūtišu “for his manhood”: idlūtum “manhood, vigor” (Harper’s glossary has EDLUTU “manhood, vigor”, ed-lu-ti-šu, at this line; the plate sign A₂ is read id here, so id-lu-ti-šu) + -šu. liddammam “let him mourn” is Harper’s DAMAMU I,2 “to lament” (a t-stem, li-id-dam-ma-am, with the ventive -am); the exact form, and the reading of idlūtum as “manhood”, are UNCERTAIN, and “mourn for his manhood” is the sense that suits the curse (the sickness unmans him before it kills him). sentences.i: May the great gods of heaven and earth, the Anunnaki, in their assembly
sentences.n: The next paragraph calls the great gods as a body. ilâni rabûti “the great gods”: DINGIR (the AN sign alone) and GAL.GAL, as at xl 40 (epilogue-1). ša šamê u erṣetim “of heaven and earth” (ša-me-e, ir-ṣi-tim). {d}A.NUN.NA is the Anunnaki, the gods as a college (the prologue spells it out syllabically). ina puḫrišunu “in their assembly”: puḫrum “assembly” + -šunu; the plate writes puḫri as a compound sign (ŠU with a box sign, as in Harper’s sign list no. 138, puḫru, in modern notation ŠU.NIGIN); I key it ŠU.LAGAB, and the second sign is TENTATIVE. The verb of the sentence is lirurū at xliv 83, and it has several objects before it.

sentences.i: the wall (?) of the house, the brickwork of Ebabbar, him, his seed, his land, his army, his people and his troops,
sentences.n: A list of objects, with a first stretch that I cannot construe; I give the words and say what is unclear. še-it bi-tim: Harper’s šêt bîtim; šēt is his ŠĒTU “wall (?)” (his query), so “the wall (?) of the house”, UNCERTAIN, and bītim is “of the house”. libit Ebabbara “the brickwork of Ebabbar”: SIG₄ is libittum (as libit Esagila at xli 48, TENTATIVE sign) and É.BABBAR.RA is Ebabbar, Šamaš’s temple (the glossary’s Ebabbar, with the ending RA). šuāti is the accusative of šū, which Harper glosses “that” (demonstrative, here and at xliv 19): “that (one)” or “him”; I do not know whether it points to the wrongdoer, to the brickwork or to the whole phrase, so I render “him” as at xliv 19 and leave it open. zēršu mātassu ṣābašu nišīšu u ummānšu “his seed, his land, his army, his people and his troops”: five objects (ZIR + -šu; mātassu as before; ERIN₂ + -šu, Harper’s sign list no. 152; nišū + -šu; ummānum + -šu, written syllabically); their verb is lirurū at xliv 83.

sentences.i: Ellil, with his mouth that is never changed, may he curse him, and
sentences.n: A last god. {d}EN.LÍL is Ellil, the name of xl 11 and xlii 53 (epilogue-1 and -2): the divine determinative, EN and the sign KID (LÍL). Harper normalizes the group Bêl, and his sign list (no. 49, the line “Bêl”) draws EN with a following box sign, as on the plate. ina pîšu “with his mouth” (the sign KA, pûm, + -šu). ša lā uttakkaru “which is not changed”: ša, lā and the D-t present of nakārum with the -u of the clause (ut-ta-ak-ka-ru, the UD sign read ut), the same verb as uttakkaru at xlii 53 (epilogue-2): his spoken word is never altered. liruršuma “let him curse him, and”: the precative lirur of arārum + -šu “him” + -ma “and” (li-ru-ur-šu-ma; no long vowel is written, so it is short, as in lirur). Line 88 has a second tier on the plate (Harper’s {b} inside ut-ta-ak-ka-ru).

sentences.i: and may the curse overtake him quickly.
sentences.n: arḫiš “quickly” (the adverb of the glossary). likšudaššu “let it overtake him”: the precative of kašādum “to reach, overtake” with the ventive -am and -šu fused (li-ik-šu-da-šu; the IG sign read ik); the subject is Ellil’s curse. The text of the stele ends with this word; Harper’s last plate has nothing after it.

glossary.apum: reed-bed, thicket, canebrake (Harper’s abu “cane, reeds”): apim (a-bi-im, BI read pi₂ or bi, genitive) in ša apim “of the reed thicket”; the form could also be abim “of the father”, which does not fit
glossary.arārum: to curse (Harper’s araru I,1): lirur (li-ru-ur, precative) “let him curse” · lirurū (li-ru-ru, precative with the plural -ū) “let them curse” · liruršuma (li-ru-ur-šu-ma, precative + -šu “him” + -ma “and”) “let him curse him, and”
glossary.arḫiš: quickly, speedily (adverb in -iš, Harper’s arḫiš): ar-ḫi-iš
glossary.asûm: physician (written with the Sumerogram A.ZU, the signs A and ZU, with no ending written): asâm (accusative, read from the context) “the physician”: asâm ippal “he shall pay the physician” · noun, Sumerogram
glossary.awīlūtum: mankind, a person, the human race (Harper’s awilutu): awīlūtum (a-wi-lu-tum) in lū … ù lū awīlūtum “or any person”
glossary.ay: may not, let not (the negative-wish particle, Harper’s a “prohibitive”; written a, said ay), before a preterite: ay unakkir “may he not change”, ay ušazziq “may he not efface”, ay iršiā “may they not get”; it is not lā
glossary.ašakkum: ašakku — the name of a sickness (Harper’s asakku “disease”), written with two signs, Á and a second sign not identified (shown ?): ašakkam (Á.?, accusative) “an ašakku”; the second sign and the exact sense are UNCERTAIN
glossary.ašrum: place; ana ašrišu “to its (proper) place” · ašar “where”, with a verb in the subjunctive: ašar illiku “where he went” · ašar (a-šar, the form before a genitive) “the place of”: ašar tamḫārim “in the place of battle”
glossary.balûm: to go out (of fire); D-stem bullûm “to extinguish”: ana bullîm “to put (it) out” · to destroy, bring to an end (Harper’s balû I,1): ibêllû (i-bi-el-lu-u, present 3rd plural with the -u of a clause) “they destroy”; the exact verb is UNCERTAIN
glossary.banûm: to build, create; ibniušu “whom he created” · bānītī (ba-ni-ti, feminine participle + -ī “my”; Harper’s banîtu “mother”) “my creator”: ummum bānītī “the mother, my creator” · ibni (ib-ni, preterite, after ay) “he creates, begets”: ay ibni “may he not beget”
glossary.binûtum: Harper’s binûtu “muscle, life”; here “body” (my choice, UNCERTAIN): biniātišu (bi-ni-a-ti-šu, plural biniātu + -šu) “his body”
glossary.bēltum: lady, mistress (the feminine of bēlum): bēltiša (be-el-ti-ša) “her mistress”; bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”, from the construct bēlit + -ša, t + š said ss · bēltum written with the single sign NIN, “lady”
glossary.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone · bīssu (É-ba(=zu): the plate sign is BA where ZU is meant) “his house”, the t of bītum and -šu said ss: bīssu ipuš “he has set up a house of his own”; bīt abišu “his father’s house” (É a-bi-šu), bīt written É alone
glossary.damqum: good, gracious; damiqtim “gracious” · damqātišu (dam-qa₂-ti-šu, feminine plural damqātum + -šu) “his good things” · damiqtum (da-mi-iq-tum, feminine nominative, IG read iq) “gracious”: lamassī damiqtum “my gracious guardian spirit”
glossary.damum: blood: dāmīšunu (da-mi-šu-nu, plural dāmū, here accusative dāmī, + -šunu) “their blood”
glossary.damāmum: to lament, mourn (Harper’s damāmu I,2, a t-stem): liddammam (li-id-dam-ma-am, precative with the ventive -am) “let him mourn”; the exact form is UNCERTAIN
glossary.dannum: the strong one: ina dīnim ana dannim ištarak “in a lawsuit he handed (him) to the strong” · strong, mighty (adjective): dannim (genitive) “strong”, danniātim (da-ni-a-tim, feminine plural genitive) “mighty”
glossary.dumqum: kindness, favour (Harper’s dumqu): dumqīya (dum-qi₂-ia, KI read qi₂) “my kindness”; qābiat dumqīya “who speaks of my kindness”, UNCERTAIN as an idiom
glossary.eli: against, upon · with suffixes: elišu, eliša, elišunu “upon him, her, them” (of a debt)
glossary.erṣetum: earth, land, territory: erṣetišunu “their territory” · erṣetim (ir-ṣi-tim, genitive) “of earth”: šamê u erṣetim “of heaven and earth”, ina erṣetim “in the earth” · erṣetīšu (ir-ṣi-ti-šu) “his land”
glossary.ezzum: furious, raging (Harper’s ezzu, adverb ezziš “furiously”) · izziš (iz-zi-iš, with i for e, adverb in -iš) “furiously” · izzitim (iz-zi-tim, feminine genitive; Harper’s ez-zi-tim) “fierce”: išātim izzitim “of fierce fire”
glossary.gurunnum: heap, pile (Harper’s gurunnu): gurun (gu-ru-un, the form before a genitive) “a heap of”: gurun šalmat “a heap of corpses”
glossary.idlūtum: manhood, vigour (Harper’s edlūtu “manhood, vigor”, ed-lu-ti-šu): idlūtišu (id-lu-ti-šu, the A₂ sign read id) “his manhood”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods” · ilum (the AN sign alone, DINGIR) “the god”, the god not named in the line · ilī (written NI.NI, two triangle signs, Harper’s List no. 99) “gods”: irrīt ilī “the curse of the gods”, abu ilī “father of the gods”
glossary.imittum: right side, right hand: imnīya (im-ni-ia, imittum + -ia) “my right”: ālik imnīya “who goes at my right”
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year” · “with, by”, of company or means (UNCERTAIN): ina liātim “with (or by) the cattle” · also “with, by means of” (ina kakkim dannim “with the mighty weapon”, ina igigallim “with wisdom”), “by” with kibīt “command” and awāt “word” (the authority), “in” a manner (ina damiqtim “in favor”, ina šulmim “in peace”)
glossary.irnittum: victory (Harper’s irnittu): irnitti (ir-ni-ti, the form before a genitive) “victory of”
glossary.irritum: curse (Harper’s irritu): irrītīya (ir-ri-ti-ia) “my curses” (with -ia “my”) · irrīt (ir-ri-it, the form before a genitive) “the curse of” · irrītim (ir-ri-tim, genitive) “of the curse”: aššum irrītim šināti “because of those curses” · irritam (ir-ri-tam, accusative) “a curse”, the cognate object of arārum: irritam marūštam lirurū “let them curse with a grievous curse” · irrītim (ir-ri-tim, genitive, here taken as a plural) “curses”: irrītim danniātim “with mighty curses”
glossary.izuzzum-Š: Š-stem of izuzzum “to stand”: to make stand, set up · lišziz (li-iš-zi-iz, Š precative) “let him set up”: nakiršu elīšu lišziz “let him set his enemy up against him”
glossary.išātum: fire: išātum innapiḫma “fire broke out”; ana išātim “into the fire”
glossary.išītum: confusion (Harper’s išîtu “confusion, revolt”): išītam (i-ši-tam, accusative) “confusion”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.kabtum: heavy; grave (of an offence): arnam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a heavy offence” · of a wound, severe: ṣimmam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a severe wound”
glossary.kakkum: weapon: kakkim (GIŠ.TUKUL, Sumerogram, no ending written; genitive after ina) “of the weapon”; Harper’s glossary gives no spelling, and the second sign (keyed TUK) is TENTATIVE · kakkašu, kakkišu (GIŠ.TUKUL-šu, Sumerogram + -šu) “his weapon”; kakkīya (GIŠ.TUKUL-ia) “my weapons”
glossary.kamûm: to bind (the verb behind Harper’s KAMÎŠ “bound”): kamiš (ka-mi-iš, adverb in -iš; Harper has KAMÎŠ “bound” as its own entry) “bound, in bonds”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.kašādum: to reach, overcome: iktašassu “(the River) has overcome him” · likšussu (li-ik-šu-zu, precative + -šu, the d and š said ss, written ZU) “let it reach him, overtake him” · likšudaššu (li-ik-šu-da-šu, precative + the ventive -am + -šu “him”, the m said š) “let it overtake him”: arḫiš likšudaššu “let it overtake him quickly”
glossary.kašādum-Š: Š-stem of kašādum: to cause to reach: uštakšidaššu “he got him back (to his city)” · mušakšidu (mu-ša-ak-ši-du, participle, the -u kept) “who brings about, who gives”: mušakšidu irnittīya “who brings about my victory”
glossary.kašūšum: Harper’s kašûšu “power, strength”: kašūšišu (ka-šu-ši-šu, kašūšum + -šu, genitive) “his kašūšu, his might”; the sense is UNCERTAIN (a name for a divine weapon is also possible)
glossary.kirbītum: midst (Harper’s kirbitu): kirbit (kir-bi-it, the form before a genitive) “the midst of”: ina kirbit nišīšu “in the midst of his people”; UNCERTAIN as a word
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house” · in place of, for (of animal for animal): alpam kīma alpim “an ox for an ox” (the §263 restitution)
glossary.lamassum: the lamassu — protective guardian spirit (the KAL sign) · lamassī (la-ma-zi, “my lamassu”, the zi written for -ssī): lamassī damiqtum “my gracious guardian spirit”
glossary.lamādum: to learn, to know; of a person, to know carnally (Harper): iltamad (il-ta-ma-ad, perfect) “he has known (his daughter)”; ilmassi (il-ma-zi) “he has known her” (preterite ilmad + -ši “her”, d + š said ss, spelled with the sign ZI); ilmassima (il-ma-zi-ma) “has known her, and” · ilammadu (i-lam-ma-du, present with the -u of the clause) “he knows”: kirībšu lā ilammadu “he does not know its inside”
glossary.lemnum: evil, bad: lemnam (lim-nam, accusative) “an evil omen” · lemnētim (li-im-ne-tim, feminine plural genitive) “evil things”: ana lemnētim “into evil”
glossary.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share” · libbaša, libbiša (li-ib-ba-ša, li-ib-bi-ša) “her heart”: mala libbiša “as much as her heart wants”; libbaša uṭabbū “they shall make her heart good”, i.e. content her · ša libbiša (li-ib-bi-ša) “what is in her womb”, literally “that of her heart”, the unborn child: ana ša libbiša “for what was in her womb” · libbu (li-ib-bu) in ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land” (Harper’s form; after ina one would expect libbi)
glossary.libittum: brick, brickwork (Harper’s libittu): libit (SIG₄, Sumerogram, form before a genitive: libit Esagila “the brickwork of Esagila”); the sign is TENTATIVE
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see” · before an infinitive, ana lā ḫabālim “so as not to wrong”
glossary.malûm-D: D-stem of malûm “to be full”: to fill; with ana qāt, to hand over to · limallišuma (li-ma-al-li-šu-ma, D precative + -šu “him” + -ma “and”) “let her hand him over, and”: ana qāt nakrišu limallišuma “into the hand of his enemy let her deliver him, and”
glossary.maqātum-Š: Š-stem of maqātum “to fall”: to make fall, fell · lišamqit (li-ša-am-qi₂-it, Š precative, KI read qi₂; Harper prints ki) “let her make fall”
glossary.marūštum: grievous, blighting (Harper’s marūštu): marūštum (ma-ru-uš-tum, feminine nominative) “grievous”, of a word (awātum)
glossary.marṣum: sick, ill: marṣam (mar-ṣa-am, accusative) “sick”, agreeing with its noun · adjective
glossary.maḫārum: to receive: imḫur(u) · imḫur, imḫuru “he received” (preterite; subjunctive in a clause), imaḫḫar “he shall receive” (present); …ḫari… in a broken form · to face, withstand (litany): qabal lā maḫārim “combat none can face” · imtaḫar (im-ta-ḫar) “she received” (perfect; Harper’s maḫāru I,2, “to receive”): grain and silver for beer · maḫir (ma-ḫi-ir, stative, 3rd singular) “has received”: idīšu … maḫir “he has received his wage” · imaḫḫaršu (i-maḫ-ḫar-šu, present + -šu) “he shall accept from him”: the owner of the pen imaḫḫaršu the loss, “shall accept it from him”
glossary.murṣum: illness, sickness (Harper’s murṣu): murṣam (mur-ṣa-am, accusative, HAR read mur) “an illness”: murṣam kabtam “a heavy illness”
glossary.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter” · mārtaka (DUMU.SAL-ka) “your daughter”, mārtī (DUMU.SAL-i) “my daughter”, mārtim (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) “of the daughter”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · mārtišu also written DUMU.SAL-šu (DUMU + SAL + ŠU) “his daughter”: ana mārtišu “to his daughter” · mārat (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) construct “daughter of”: mārat awīlim “a man’s daughter”, mārat muškēnim “a commoner’s daughter”
glossary.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers” · mār X (DUMU, the sign TUR) “a member of the class X”, literally “son of X”: mār ummiānim “a craftsman”, mār zinništim “the son of a woman”; māram (DUMU) “a son”, mārašu (DUMU-šu) “his son”, mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons”, mārīšu “his sons” · mārū (DUMU{meš}, plural, nominative) “sons”: mārū mātim “sons of the land”, i.e. natives, as a predicate
glossary.mātum: land, country · māt (ma-at) the form before a following genitive, “the land of”: ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country” · mātim (ma-tim, or the Sumerogram KALAM, no ending written) genitive “of the land”: ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land”, mārū mātim “natives of the country”, mātim šanītim “another country” · mātassu (ma-zu, with -šu “his”, the t and š said ss and written with ZU) “his land”; mātišu (ma-ti-šu) “his land” · mātātim (ma-ta-tim, plural genitive) “of the lands”: bēltum ṣīrtum ša mātātim “the exalted lady of the lands”
glossary.mūtum: death (mūtum; not mutum “husband”): mūt (mu-ut, the form before a genitive) “death of” · mūtim (mu-tim, genitive) “of death”: nišiq mūtim “the bite of death”
glossary.mūšum: night: mūšim (mu-ši-im, genitive) in ana mūšim “into night”
glossary.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere · of a tooth, to knock out: ittadi (it-ta-di, perfect) “he has knocked out”, inaddû (i-na-ad-du-u, present plural) “they shall knock out”: šinni awīlim ittadi “he has knocked out a man’s tooth” · addi (ad-di, preterite, 1st person) “I let drop”: aḫī ul addi “I did not let my arm drop”, the idiom of aḫšu iddi · littaddi (li-it-ta-ad-di, precative with infixed -t-, Harper’s nadû I,2; the stem is UNCERTAIN) “let her cast down”
glossary.nakārum-D: D-stem of nakārum “to be strange, different”: to make different, change: uttakkir (ut-ta-ak-ki-ir, D perfect) “he has changed”: šimtam uttakkir “he has changed the mark (?)” (the object is UNCERTAIN; the verb is plain from the stem) · after ay: ay unakkir (u-na-ak-ki-ir, D preterite) “may he not change” · uttakkaru (ut-ta-ka-ru, with the subjunctive -u; Harper files it under nakaru II,2 beside the perfect uttakkir) “is altered”, the passive of the D, UNCERTAIN: ša kibīssu lā uttakkaru “whose command is not altered”
glossary.nasāḫum-N: N-stem of nasāḫum, the passive: to be uprooted, cast out (of a family house): innassaḫ (in-na-az-za-aḫ) “he shall be cast out” · innassaḫu (in-na-za-ḫu, present with the -u of the clause, za for -ssa- as in innassaḫ) “is removed”: lā innassaḫu “which is not removed”
glossary.naḫûm-D: D-stem of naḫûm “to be quiet” (Harper’s naḫû II,1 “to pacify, to allay”): to quiet, give ease to · unaḫḫuššu (u-na-aḫ-ḫu-šu, unaḫḫuš, D present, + -šu “him”, the two š written once) “he gives him ease”: lā unaḫḫuššu “he does not give him ease”
glossary.nišqum: bite (Harper’s nišqu): nišiq (ni-ši-iq, construct, IG read iq) “the bite of”: nišiq mūtim “the bite of death”; not našāqum “to kiss”; the exact sense is UNCERTAIN
glossary.nišū: people; the household: nišīšu “his household” · nišīšu (ni-ši-šu) “his people”: nišīšu ina mīšarim lirʾi “let him shepherd his people in justice”; šīr nišīšu “the flesh of his people”
glossary.nukurtum: enmity, hostility (Harper’s glossary “enmity”): nukurtim (nu-ku-ur-tim, genitive) in ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country”, i.e. an enemy land
glossary.palûm: reign, term of rule (the BAL sign, Harper’s List no. 7, palû): palêya (BALA-ia, with -ia “my”) “my reign” · palê (BALA, before a genitive) “the reign of”: palê tanēḫim “a reign of sighing”
glossary.pašāḫum: to become calm, to calm (Harper’s pašāḫu I,1 “to be healed, to be cured”): ipaššeḫu (i-pa-aš-še-ḫu, present with the -u of a ša-clause) “(which the physician) calms”, UNCERTAIN whether transitive or intransitive
glossary.petûm: to open; of land, to bring into cultivation: iptete “he has opened” · preterite ipte, iptēma “he opened” · iptēma (ip-te-ma) “he has opened, and”, of a part of the body, with a knife · pātiat (pa-ti-a-at, feminine participle, the form before a genitive) “who opens”: pātiat kakkīya “who opens my weapons”, UNCERTAIN as a picture
glossary.pûm: mouth (the KA sign); ina pī mātim “in the mouth of the land” · ana pî ṣimdat šarrim “according to the mouth of the king’s ordinance” · ana pî riksātīšu “according to his contract”, literally “to the mouth of his binding terms” (KA read pî)
glossary.qablum: battle, combat · qablê (MURUB₄.MURUB₄, the sign doubled, plural genitive) “of combats”: taḫāzim u qablê “of battle and of combats” · qabal (qa₂-ba-al, the form before a genitive) “the battle of”: qabal lā maḫār “battle none can face”
glossary.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma · iqabbi (written i-qa₂-ab-bi-ma, iqabbi + -ma; Harper prints the GA sign as ga, read qa₂) present “he shall say, declare”: ina maḫar ilim … iqabbima “he shall declare before the god” · liqbīma (li-iq-bi-ma, li- + iqbi + -ma) “let him say, and” · liqbi (li-iq-bi, precative) “let him say”: ina pīšu kabtim liqbi “with his weighty mouth let him say”
glossary.qamûm: to burn (Harper’s kamû I,1 “to burn”, li-ik-me; the form is UNCERTAIN): liqme (li-iq-me, IG read iq, precative) “let him burn”
glossary.qatûm-Š: Š-stem of qatûm “to come to an end” (Harper’s qatû III,1): to bring to an end, cut off · lišaqti (li-ša-aq-ti, Š precative; AK read aq) “let him bring to an end” · lišaqtišuma (li-ša-ti-šu-ma, precative + -šu “him” + -ma “and”) “let him bring him to an end, and”: the spelling has no aq (Harper’s glossary has li-ša-[ak]-ti-šu, the aq bracketed), so the form is UNCERTAIN: ina kakkišu dannim lišaqtišuma “with his strong weapon let him bring him to an end (?), and”
glossary.qātum: hand: ina qāt “from the hand of” · qātīšu (qa₂-ti-šu) “of his hands”: bīš qātīšu “his own goods” · qāt (qa₂-at) construct “in the hand of, in the care of”: ina qāt mušēniqtim “in the care (hand) of the wet-nurse” · qātīšu “of his hands” in šipir qātīšu “the work of his hands” · ina qātišu (qa₂-ti-šu) “in his hand”: ittaṣbat ina qātišu “he was caught with it in his hand” · qāssu (qa₂-zu, with -šu “his”, the ss written with ZU) “his hand”
glossary.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone” · rabītišu (ra-bi-ti-šu) “his senior one”, the feminine with -šu: read as the father’s chief wife, UNCERTAIN · rabîm (ra-bi-im, genitive) “great”: ina kašūšišu rabîm “by his great kašūšu” · rabêtim (ra-be-a-tim, feminine plural genitive) “great”: ina uzzatiša rabêtim “in her great wrath” · rabûti (GAL.GAL, plural) “great”: ilāni rabûti “the great gods”
glossary.rašûm-Š: to cause to acquire (Š-stem of rašûm “to acquire, get”; double accusative): ušaršušu (u-šar-šu-šu) “who has made him acquire (children)” (ušarši + the subjunctive -u + -šu “him”); the analysis of the ending is UNCERTAIN · ušaršišināti (u-šar-ši-ši-na-ti, 1st person) “I let them get”: mugallitam ul ušaršišināti “I let no molester have them” · ušarši (u-šar-ši, preterite, after ay) “she lets (him) obtain”, ušaršīšu (u-šar-ši-šu, + -šu “him”): ay ušarši šuāti “may she not let him obtain”; šumam ay ušaršīšu “may she not let him obtain a name”
glossary.râmum: to love: irammu (i-ra-am-mu, present), with the subjunctive -u after ša: ša irammu “whom he/she loves” · rāʾimat (ra-i-ma-at, feminine participle, the form before a genitive) “who loves”: rāʾimat palêya “who loves my reign”
glossary.rêʾûm-pasture: to pasture, graze (a herd): the infinitive in the genitive after ana, ana … rēʾîm “to pasture” (ri-im), said rēʾîm; the spelling ri-im is Harper’s and the reading of the word as the infinitive of rêʾûm (the verb behind rēʾûm “shepherd”) is my own from the grammar, UNCERTAIN · lirʾi (li-ri, precative) “let him shepherd”: nišīšu ina mīšarim lirʾi “let him shepherd his people in justice”; the spelling li-ri has no sign for the ʾ, and Harper files it under another verb (ARU II,1 “to carry, to rule”), so the reading is UNCERTAIN · lirʾûšu (li-ru-šu, 3rd plural precative + -šu “him”, the ʾ not written) “let them herd him”, of a captive led away, UNCERTAIN (Harper files li-ru-šu under aru II,1 “to carry, to rule”)
glossary.saḫmaštum: revolt, rebellion (Harper’s saḫmaštu, filed under S): saḫmaštam (za-aḫ-ma-aš-tam, ZA read sa, accusative) “revolt”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.tamḫārum: battle (UD read tam): tamḫārim (tam-ḫa-ri-im, genitive) “of battle”: ašar tamḫārim “in the place of battle”
glossary.taḫāzum: battle, conflict (Harper’s taḫāzu): taḫāzim “of battle”, written with the single sign AK (Harper’s sign list no. 48); which Sumerogram it is I do not know, so the reading from his normalization and the sense are UNCERTAIN; the key AK is the sign’s shape only
glossary.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr · litēršu (li-te-ir-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s taru II,1) “let him turn back / take back from him”, UNCERTAIN: melam šarrūtim litēršu “let him turn the glory of kingship away from him” · litēr (li-te-ir, precative, without a suffix) “let him turn”: ana tīl abūbim litēr “let him turn (it) into a mound of the flood” · litēršum (li-te-ir-šum, precative + -šum “for him”) and litēršumma (li-te-ir-šum-ma, + -ma “and”) “let him turn (it) for him”: ūmam ana mūšim litēršumma “let him turn the day into night for him” · litēršuma (li-te-ir-šu-ma, precative + -šu “from him” + -ma “and”) “let her turn (a son) away from him, and”, UNCERTAIN as litēršu above
glossary.ummum: mother: ana ummišu “to his mother”, ummašu urabbāšu “his mother shall raise him” · ummātim (um-ma-tim) plural “mothers”: ana ummātim “by mothers”; ummātišunu “their mothers”
glossary.ummānum: army, host: ummānišu (um-ma-ni-šu) “his army”; išid ummānišu “the foundation of his army” · ummānšu (um-ma-an-šu) “his troops”; ummānātišu (um-ma-na-ti-šu, plural ummānāt + -šu) “his troops”
glossary.uzzatum: wrath, anger: uzzatiša (uz-za-ti-ša, uzzatum + -ša, genitive; the adjective with it is plural, so the noun is read as a plural of intensity) “her wrath”: ina uzzatiša rabêtim “in her great wrath”
glossary.waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation” · ušeṣṣûšu (u-še-iz-zu-u-šu) “they shall make him go out” (present plural + -šu “him”; Harper writes ṣ as z): ālam ušeṣṣûšu “they shall drive him out of the city” · šuṣâ (šu-ṣa-a; Harper’s su-sa-a, under III,1) “brought out (?)”: the form (a stative plural? an imperative?) and its subject are UNCERTAIN · lišaṣiaššumma (li-ša-ṣi-a-aš-šum-ma, Š precative + the ventive -am + -šum “for him” + -ma “and”) “let her bring out for him, and”: ina biniātišu lišaṣiaššumma “let her make (them) break out on him in his body, and”
glossary.zērum: seed; offspring (written with the seed-sign NUMUN) · zēr šeʾim (ŠE.ZIR, the logogram ŠE + ZIR) “seed-grain”
glossary.ša: who, which, of · also “whose”: ša + a noun with its own suffix + the verb at the end (ša ḫaṭṭašu išarat “whose scepter is straight”), the verb in the subjunctive
glossary.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind · iššakkan also written iš-ta-ak-ka-an (Harper’s reading, UNCERTAIN): andurār amtim iššakkan “the release of the slave-woman shall be established” · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be set”: andurāršunu iššakkan “their release shall be set” · šaknāt (ša-ak-na-at, feminine plural stative) “those set (with)”: šaknāt napištim “those set with life”, i.e. those who have life, UNCERTAIN · liškunšum (li-iš-ku-un-šum, G precative + -šum) “let him set for him”
glossary.šalmatum: corpse (feminine of šalmum): šalmat (ša-al-ma-at, the form before a genitive) “corpse of”, in gurun šalmat ummānātišu “a heap of the corpses of his troops”
glossary.šaqûm: to give to drink; Š-stem — mušešqi “who waters” · lišqi (li-iš-qi₂, G precative, KI read qi₂) “let her give to drink”: erṣetam lišqi “let her make the earth drink”
glossary.šebērum: to break: ištebir (iš-te-bi-ir, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has broken”, išebbirū (i-še-ib-bi-ru, present, 3rd plural, with the b doubled) “they shall break” · verb · išbir (iš-bi-ir, preterite, 3rd singular) “he has broken” · lišbir (li-iš-bi-ir, precative) “let him break”: ḫaṭṭašu lišbir “let him break his scepter”
glossary.šuāti: that, the aforesaid · as the independent pronoun “him”: šuāti u bīšašu “him and his goods”
glossary.šētum: wall (?) (Harper’s šētu, with his query): šēt (še-it, construct) in šēt bītim “the wall (?) of the house”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days” · ina ūmim (i-na UD) “per day, by the day”, with the numeral 1{kam}: ina ūmim 1{kam} 180 qa “for each day 180 qa”; the day-rate formula of §271–277 · ūmī (the sign UD alone) “days”: ūmī iṣūtim “few days” · ūmī (UD-mi) “days” in a list with arḫī “months” and šanāt “years”; ūm (UD-um) “day(s) of” before a genitive: ūm balāṭīya “the days of my life”
glossary.ḫapāšum: to break, crush, shatter (Harper’s ḫapāšu I,1): liḫpuš (li-iḫ-pu-uš, G precative) “let him smash”
glossary.ṣalmum: statue, image (Harper’s salmu): ṣalmīya (ALAN-ia) “my statue”; the sign ALAN is TENTATIVE, the word being unspelled in Harper’s glossary · ṣalam (ṣa-lam, the form before a genitive) “image of”: ṣalam ṭīṭim “an image of clay”
glossary.ṣimdum: bandage (Harper’s simdu, written zi-im-di with ZI read ṣi): ṣimdi (ṣi-im-di, genitive) “by a bandage”, in ina ṣimdi; not ṣimdatum “ordinance”
glossary.ṣimmum: wound (Harper’s sense), UNCERTAIN, not derivable from the grammar: ṣimmam (ṣi-im-ma-am, accusative) “a wound”; the first sign is the sign ZI in the autograph (Harper prints zi-im-ma-am here), read ṣi · noun, sense uncertain
glossary.ṣābum: troops, soldiery (the sign ERIM): ṣāb nisḫātim “struck-off troops”
glossary.ṣērum: the open country, the steppe: ina ṣērim “in the open country”
glossary.ṣīrum: lofty, exalted · ṣīrtum (ṣi-ir-tum, feminine nominative) “exalted”: bēltum ṣīrtum “the exalted lady”
glossary.ṭīṭum: clay (the plate has two DI signs, read ṭi-ṭi; Harper prints di-di-im): ṭīṭim (ṭi-ṭi-im, genitive) “of clay”: ṣalam ṭīṭim “an image of clay”
